A0227.title: Teleoperation Channel Encryption & Authentication
A0227.definition: End-to-end encryption, mutual certificate authentication, command-sequence anti-replay, and latency-anomaly detection on robot teleoperation (teleop) control channels to prevent hijacking, replay, or injection.
A0227.description:
Teleoperation channel encryption & authentication builds four layers of defense for the remote-control links of humanoid, surgical, and hazardous-operation robots. First, end-to-end encryption keeps control commands encrypted in transit, preventing man-in-the-middle eavesdropping and tampering. Second, mutual certificate authentication has the operator side and robot side verify each other's certificates, blocking unauthorized parties. Third, command sequence numbers and timestamps — each command carries a monotonically increasing sequence number, and the receiver verifies freshness, resisting action replay. Fourth, latency-anomaly detection — teleoperation is latency-sensitive, and injected abnormal latency destabilizes fine operations; detecting latency jitter identifies delay-injection attacks.

This measure is the core defense direction after the Raven II surgical-robot hijacking and similar incidents; it belongs to the communication-security system together with A0118 (certificate-based device authentication) and A0150 (OTA channel encryption and integrity), specialized for the low-latency and anti-replay needs of real-time control channels.
A0227.limitation: Encryption and authentication add communication latency affecting real-time fine teleoperation (e.g., remote surgery); certificate and key management is complex, requiring timely revocation on device loss or personnel change; cannot defend insiders with legitimate credentials; latency detection may false-positive under normal network fluctuation.
